label: Aggregate equity-premium valuation/macro timing
scope: US and international aggregate equity markets
summary: Dividend yields and classic macro predictors show in-sample association, but recursive OOS tests usually fail to beat the historical mean. Combinations and economic restrictions salvage only small, fragile gains.
positive_evidence: Campbell-Thompson restrictions and Rapach combinations produce small POOS utility gains in some windows.
negative_evidence: Goyal-Welch find most predictors fail OOS versus the historical mean; later updates remain largely adverse. Goyal-Welch-Zafirov (2024) re-examine 29 newer predictors and find the large majority fail out-of-sample, reaffirming the adverse baseline.
key_caveat: Cheap and scalable, but incremental OOS value over buy-and-hold/historical mean is weak and unstable.

label: Equity value (book-to-market and related)
scope: US and international equities, diversified long-short or long-only sleeves
summary: Value organizes the cross-section across countries and long histories. Premia decay and droughts are material, but the theme remains among the more reproducible equity characteristics.
positive_evidence: International and Bayesian global replications retain value as a broad theme under standardized construction.
negative_evidence: Hou-Xue-Zhang show many related published variants fail conservative standardized tests; droughts and definition sensitivity remain.
key_caveat: Production candidate as a patient diversified sleeve, not a standalone guarantee; crowding and definition choice matter.

label: Standalone equity size premium
summary: Historical size effects concentrate in microcaps and illiquid names. After value-weighting, costs, and later samples, standalone size is weak.
positive_evidence: Original Fama-French evidence and some size-related patterns in early samples.
negative_evidence: Microcap dependence and trading costs remove most standalone value under conservative construction.
key_caveat: Reject as a standalone premium; residual size exposure is usually a liquidity/microcap artifact.

label: Low-volatility / betting-against-beta / low-risk investing
target: cross-sectional risk-adjusted returns of low- vs high-risk stocks
scope: US and international single-stock universes; BAB extensions to Treasuries, credit, and futures
summary: Low-beta and low-volatility stocks earn higher risk-adjusted returns than the CAPM predicts — a gross pattern reproduced across nine decades, 20+ markets, and several asset classes. External re-examination shows the flagship BAB construction leans on nano-cap rank-weighting, an artifact-prone beta estimator, and unmodeled costs, leaving a smaller value-weighted defensive premium with no significant net alpha over modern factor models.
positive_evidence: Frazzini-Pedersen BAB earns 0.70%/month (t=7.12) over 1926-2012, significant in each 20-year subperiod, with positive Sharpe in 18 of 19 countries and analogous premia in Treasuries and credit; Baker-Bradley-Wurgler document the long-horizon low-volatility return gap.
negative_evidence: Novy-Marx-Velikov (EXT) show rank-weighting is a backdoor to nano-cap equal-weighting, value-weighted BAB has an insignificant FF5 alpha (24 bp, t=1.63), and 60 bp/month costs cut profitability by more than half, leaving insignificant net alpha; Fama-French 2016 largely subsume the effect via profitability/investment exposures.
key_caveat: The gross anomaly is one of the best-replicated in finance, but the tradable net-of-cost incremental alpha of the tested long-short implementations is not established; long-only low-vol variants avoid shorting and leverage frictions but face benchmark-constraint capacity limits and post-2011 crowding concerns.

label: Cross-sectional equity momentum
summary: Intermediate-horizon winners continue to outperform losers across markets. The pattern is among the most replicated equity signals, but crashes, turnover, borrow, and capacity are first-order.
positive_evidence: Broad international replication and Bayesian global theme evidence; liquidity-aware implementations can preserve capacity at institutional scale in some studies.
negative_evidence: Lesmond et al. argue profits concentrate in costly stocks; high turnover and crash risk remain material.
key_caveat: Production candidate only with explicit crash controls, borrow, and turnover governance.

label: Profitability / quality / conservative investment
summary: Profitability and related quality/investment themes complement value, survive in larger stocks, and appear in later factor models and global replications.
positive_evidence: q-factor spanning, Fama-French five-factor profitability/investment, and global theme replication.
negative_evidence: Accounting definitions are flexible; some related anomalies weaken in historical backcasts.
key_caveat: Best used inside a diversified multifactor sleeve with low-turnover construction.

label: Published equity anomaly zoo (indiscriminate)
summary: Hundreds of published predictors reproduce under original definitions but mostly fail after multiple testing, microcap controls, costs, and post-publication decay. Numerical reproduction is not economic replication.
positive_evidence: Chen-Zimmermann show high computational reproduction; Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen find broad themes persist internationally.
negative_evidence: Hou-Xue-Zhang, McLean-Pontiff, and Green-Hand-Zhang show most individual anomalies fail conservative, post-publication, or multivariate tests.
key_caveat: Reject indiscriminate anomaly selection; evaluate diversified themes, not the average published signal.

label: Cross-sectional equity machine learning
summary: Trees and neural nets improve retrospective OOS prediction over linear baselines, mainly by recombining momentum, liquidity, and volatility signals. Feature-publication look-ahead, turnover, and costs materially shrink net value.
positive_evidence: Gu-Kelly-Xiu, China ML, and some international ML studies report strong chronological OOS prediction.
negative_evidence: Avramov et al. and Li-Rossi-Yan-Zheng show profits concentrate in hard-to-arbitrage stocks and curated features; recent decades and annual horizons are weaker.
key_caveat: Research-to-specialist transition only; no audited LIVE-X net alpha.

label: Short-term equity reversal
summary: Prior-month losers outperform winners in gross returns. The effect is largely a liquidity-provision premium that requires exceptional execution.
positive_evidence: Robust gross replication across decades.
negative_evidence: Extremely high turnover and bid-ask/impact consumption for non-specialists.
key_caveat: Specialist liquidity-provision strategy, not a generic retail alpha.

label: Long-horizon equity reversal
summary: Multi-year loser/winner reversal appears in discovery samples but is sensitive to microcaps, distress, and risk adjustment.
positive_evidence: De Bondt-Thaler discovery evidence and related overreaction interpretations.
negative_evidence: Historical backcasts and conservative replications weaken many long-horizon accounting/reversal claims.
key_caveat: Weak diversifier at best after risk and microcap controls.

label: Equity-index / liquid futures time-series trend
summary: Own-return trend is positive across liquid futures over long histories. Much headline performance depends on volatility scaling and simulated costs; asset-level slopes are weaker than portfolio results.
positive_evidence: Cross-asset historical evidence and related managed-futures/theme support. Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen extend trend evidence to a century across markets (practitioner study; disclosed construction).
negative_evidence: Volatility-scaling attribution and later reanalyses temper asset-level predictability claims. Huang-Li-Wang-Zhou (2020) argue TSMOM per se is not statistically distinct from a simple mean effect once pooled, a direct challenge to the flagship study.
key_caveat: Conditional production candidate in liquid futures with disciplined risk controls; not LIVE-X audited for a single academic rule.

label: Generic equity technical trading rules
summary: Technical-rule searches show apparent profits that weaken under data-snooping controls, persistence tests, and transaction costs. Late-sample LSTM edges also decay.
positive_evidence: Early in-sample technical-rule studies and some technical-diffusion forecast papers report gross improvements.
negative_evidence: Multiple-testing/overfitting frameworks and late-sample decay eliminate most apparent profitability after costs.
key_caveat: Reject the generic profitability claim for mined technical rules.

label: Equity calendar / seasonal effects
summary: Same-calendar-month and related seasonal patterns recur internationally, but net capacity and untouched live evidence are insufficient.
positive_evidence: Heston-Sadka and Keloharju et al. document recurring seasonal continuation.
negative_evidence: Many calendar lags, high turnover for stock-level implementations, and weak live net evidence.
key_caveat: Weak conditional signal; not a standalone strategy.

label: Post-earnings-announcement drift and corporate-event predictability
target: cross-sectional stock returns after earnings announcements
horizon: H3-H4 (days to one quarter after announcement)
scope: US equities, SUE-sorted long-short portfolios around quarterly earnings announcements
summary: SUE-sorted drift is among the most replicated equity findings: roughly 4% per quarter gross hedge returns, concentrated around subsequent announcements in the exact pattern of seasonal earnings autocorrelation. Realistic spread, impact, and borrow costs consume most-to-all of the paper profits, and the drift has retreated to microcaps and largely disappeared in post-2006 samples.
positive_evidence: Bernard-Thomas document ~4%/quarter POOS hedge returns with the drift matching the +,+,+,- earnings-autocorrelation signature at the next four announcements and positive t+1 hedge returns in all 13 years; Chordia et al. independently confirm the gross drift on 1972-2005 data.
negative_evidence: Chordia et al. find spread, market-impact, and borrow costs account for 70-100% of paper profits with a $5M position unprofitable; post-publication tests find PEAD absent outside microcaps since about 2006 and in microcaps since about 2016.
key_caveat: The behavioral finding (delayed response to earnings news) is historically well established; the tradable edge is not — net value was confined to tiny capacity in illiquid names and has since decayed toward zero.

label: Financial news / filings text signals (equities)
scope: US equities with news, filings, or calls
summary: Domain-specific text measures contain short-horizon information beyond generic dictionaries. Durable net alpha after latency, licensing, and turnover remains unproven.
positive_evidence: Tetlock, Loughran-McDonald, and supervised news-text studies report chronological OOS associations.
negative_evidence: High turnover, proprietary feeds, LLM look-ahead risk, and incomplete impact/borrow treatment dominate deployability.
key_caveat: Credible event-specific information; not established as scalable live alpha.

label: Generic LLM / agentic equity investing
scope: US equities and LLM trading agents
summary: Pre-cutoff LLM backtests are contaminated by memorization. Long-horizon and live-paper benchmarks generally fail to beat passive strategies consistently.
positive_evidence: Some short post-cutoff headline studies report positive next-day associations.
negative_evidence: Memorization audits, look-ahead benches, FINSABER long-run tests, FinBen trading weakness, and M6 live-paper results are adverse for broad LLM investing claims.
key_caveat: Point-in-time models remain research-grade; generic LLM investing is not established.

label: Government yield / curve point forecasts
scope: US Treasuries and related sovereign curves
summary: Random walk / no-change is hard to beat at short horizons. Parsimonious curve models and no-arbitrage DNS variants help mainly at medium/long horizons.
positive_evidence: Diebold-Li and AFNS improve some medium-horizon forecasts; FAVAR can help with broad macro information.
negative_evidence: Short-horizon random-walk competitiveness and regime sensitivity.
key_caveat: Forecast accuracy gains do not automatically imply portfolio value.

label: Treasury excess-return / term-premium predictors
summary: Forward-rate and macro-augmented premium models are strong in sample. Post-publication and size-corrected tests find much weaker incremental value beyond yield PCs.
positive_evidence: CP, Cieslak-Povala, Gargano combinations, and corrected ML report POOS improvements in some designs.
negative_evidence: Thornton-Valente, Bauer-Hamilton, and Sarno economic-value tests are largely adverse for static extra-curve predictors.
key_caveat: Reject static standalone CP-style timing; state-adaptive combinations remain promising but not independently live-validated.

label: Government-bond carry / roll-down
summary: Ex-ante carry including roll-down predicts returns across markets. Historical evidence is broad, but public LIVE-X capacity tests are absent.
positive_evidence: Koijen et al. carry across assets; related global factor and bond-trend evidence.
negative_evidence: Recession, liquidity, and volatility exposures; no audited live public record for a single rule.
key_caveat: Conditional accept in liquid futures/cash implementations with risk budgeting.

label: Expert interest-rate survey forecasts
summary: Surveys help identify expectations and can enter successful combinations, but long-yield survey superiority as standalone alpha is weak.
positive_evidence: Surveys improve term-structure identification and enter some successful combinations.
negative_evidence: Limited evidence that surveys alone beat no-change for long yields in tradable settings.
key_caveat: Useful as information, not as a proven standalone alpha source.

label: Corporate default / distress ranking
summary: Dynamic market and accounting hazards provide strong OOS default ranking. This is underwriting/risk accuracy, not bond-trading alpha.
positive_evidence: Multiple independent hazard/distress models with chronological holdouts. E is scored on the risk-forecast carve-out basis: misclassification/decision-loss value of default ranking for underwriting and risk management, not tradable alpha.
negative_evidence: Rare-event calibration drift; Merton DD is not uniquely superior to simpler market-based scores.
key_caveat: Accept for risk ranking; do not equate with corporate-bond long-short alpha.

label: Corporate-bond factor zoo / momentum
summary: After correcting price measurement, look-ahead filters, and OTC costs/delays, most published corporate-bond factors and momentum claims fail.
positive_evidence: Early momentum and practitioner factor papers report gross/cost-adjusted positives in historical samples.
negative_evidence: Retraction of Bai-Bali-Wen; Dickerson replications and capacity studies erase most incremental alpha, especially high-turnover signals.
key_caveat: Reject the broad corporate-bond anomaly library after bias and cost correction.

label: Slow corporate credit-spread value / quality
summary: Issuer-quality and slow spread-value themes are more plausible than high-turnover factors. Capacity is higher for low-turnover credit risk, but independent sealed validation remains limited.
positive_evidence: Issuer-quality predictability; some surviving spread-value signals after correction; low-turnover capacity evidence.
negative_evidence: Most of the factor zoo fails; Kelly et al. lack independent fresh replication.
key_caveat: Conditional only for slow, liquid, low-turnover constructions.

label: Structured-credit rating / collateral surveillance
summary: Issue-time rating overrides and disclosure quality predict later deterioration. Useful for underwriting surveillance, not a liquid public alpha claim.
positive_evidence: Griffin-Tang: larger subjective AAA overrides predict worse subsequent performance.
negative_evidence: Crisis-era products and proprietary agency data; no tradable secondary-market alpha test in the ledger.
key_caveat: Accept as underwriting evidence; not a trading strategy rating.

label: Bilateral FX spot macro / Taylor-rule models
scope: Major and some EM dollar pairs
summary: No structural model uniformly dominates the random walk. Taylor-rule and related models produce pockets of POOS success that are specification- and period-dependent.
positive_evidence: Molodtsova-Papell and some long-horizon Mark-style results; survey expectations literature notes pockets.
negative_evidence: Meese-Rogoff and Cheung et al. show no uniform MSPE superiority to no-change.
key_caveat: Do not treat FX spot forecasting as a solved problem.

label: FX carry (carry-inclusive returns)
summary: Forward-discount carry earns historically positive returns after quoted spreads but with crash exposure. Post-publication and regime stability remain contested.
positive_evidence: Large historical literature with risk-premium interpretations and some net quoted-cost survival.
negative_evidence: Crash/peso risk and later decay/regime sensitivity.
key_caveat: Historically informative, not currently established effective under the strict live/cost/stability standard.

label: Currency momentum / trend
summary: Cross-sectional currency momentum is historically distinct from carry, but spreads in EM currencies and later-sample decay are severe.
positive_evidence: Menkhoff et al. historical momentum; related futures trend evidence.
negative_evidence: Bid-ask erosion and technical-rule decay in majors.
key_caveat: Not established currently after decay and cost adjustments.

label: FX order-flow forecasting
scope: Major FX pairs with proprietary dealer/customer flow
summary: Order flow explains and sometimes forecasts short-horizon FX moves, but signals are proprietary, samples are short, and capacity is unclear. Some classic exercises use non-implementable contemporaneous/future flow.
positive_evidence: Rime-Sarno-Sojli report POOS portfolio-utility gains from order flow.
negative_evidence: Evans-Lyons contemporaneous designs are not tradable forecasts; proprietary data block independent replication.
key_caveat: Promising but inaccessible at the stated evidence level for most investors.

label: Intraday/generic FX technical rules
summary: Gross technical regularities often fail after realistic hours and transaction costs; later samples show decay.
positive_evidence: Earlier technical-rule literature reported gross profits.
negative_evidence: Olson decay/cost results are adverse for net OOS profitability.
key_caveat: Ineffective in the tested liquid-major scopes, not a universal proof against every adaptive method.

label: Commodity futures curve / basis / basis-momentum
summary: Basis and basis-momentum organize historical futures premia for storables. Post-financialization decay and capacity remain unresolved.
positive_evidence: Storage-theory and basis-momentum historical evidence.
negative_evidence: Later strategy compression and no sealed live record.
key_caveat: Historically informative for storables; not established currently.

label: Commodity futures momentum / trend
summary: Cross-sectional and time-series momentum have robust historical gross/net evidence that attenuates in later samples.
positive_evidence: Multiple historical momentum/curve combination studies.
negative_evidence: Post-2004 strategy compression; seasonality largely gone in recent decades.
key_caveat: Not established currently after financialization/later-sample decay.

label: Commodity hedging-pressure / positioning
summary: Early hedging-pressure pricing results conflict with later evidence that positions do not predict subsequent returns once inventories/prices are controlled.
positive_evidence: Bessembinder and related early hedging-pressure associations.
negative_evidence: Gorton-Hayashi-Rouwenhorst null for subsequent-return prediction.
key_caveat: Heterogeneous and unresolved; do not treat as a robust trading signal.

label: Commodity futures machine learning
summary: Chronological DNN/LightGBM studies report cost-adjusted positives, but independent locked replication and impact/capacity audits are missing.
positive_evidence: Rad et al. HOLD with modeled costs; Wang-Zhang LightGBM HOLD.
negative_evidence: Short test windows, architecture multiplicity, and no independent team replication.
key_caveat: Promising only; not supported pre-live.

label: Realized / GARCH / HAR volatility forecasting
summary: Volatility is strongly forecastable. HAR/RV and carefully specified GARCH remain durable baselines; universal nonlinear ML superiority is not established.
positive_evidence: Canonical RV/HAR/GARCH evidence across assets. E is scored on the risk-forecast carve-out basis: decision-loss (QLIKE/VaR/ES) value of volatility forecasts, not trading returns.
negative_evidence: Economic trading value is separate from forecast accuracy; ML gains are dataset-dependent.
key_caveat: Established as statistical risk forecasting; decision value depends on the risk-management use case. Return applications are separately contested: Moreira-Muir volatility-managed portfolios show in-sample utility gains, but Cederburg et al. find the gains largely vanish out-of-sample across factors.

label: Option-implied information for future volatility
summary: Model-free and Black-Scholes IV generally add forward-looking volatility information beyond historical measures.
positive_evidence: IV subsumes or complements historical RV across multiple markets.
negative_evidence: Statistical forecast gains are much stronger than evidence of standalone trading profits. Canina-Figlewski (1993) found S&P 100 IV a poor and biased RV forecast in their early sample — the canonical adverse result later reconciled by better data and overlapping-sample corrections.
key_caveat: Strong for volatility forecasting; weak as a claim of net option-trading alpha.

label: Variance / tail-risk premia and equity returns
summary: VRP and disaster-fear measures predict equity returns in historical samples, especially at intermediate horizons. Friction-adjusted alpha is not established.
positive_evidence: US and global VRP return predictability; crisis holdout for tail fears; SVIX-related evidence.
negative_evidence: Sample and VRP-definition sensitivity; no full implementable portfolio/cost audit.
key_caveat: Credible state variable; not established net market-timing alpha.

label: Cross-sectional equity-option return anomalies
summary: Many characteristics predict gross option returns. Independent cost reimplementations find that realistic option, stock, and hedge costs eliminate net significance for the broad set.
positive_evidence: Goyal-Saretto, Cao-Han, Zhan et al., and option ML report gross/cost-adjusted positives under assumed spreads.
negative_evidence: O’Donovan-Yu: none of 24 signals remain significant net under main cost treatment.
key_caveat: Gross predictability is real; broad net option-anomaly alpha is not established.

label: Limit-order-book / order-flow direction prediction
summary: Ultra-short-horizon statistical predictability from order flow is real but decays within events/seconds and often fails external generalization. Mid-price accuracy is not net HFT P&L.
positive_evidence: Sirignano-Cont and related deep LOB studies show directional accuracy and transfer; execution RL can help fills.
negative_evidence: Prata et al. external failure; random-split and contemporaneous OFI designs are invalid as forecasts; latency races impose real costs.
key_caveat: Statistical microstructure predictability ≠ deployable retail/HFT alpha without queue, latency, and impact evidence.

label: Cryptocurrency cross-sectional momentum
summary: Gross momentum appears in early samples but is highly sensitive to survivorship, delistings, microcaps, and costs. Survivor-only portfolios are not tradeable.
positive_evidence: Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu factor evidence in early samples.
negative_evidence: Ammann survivorship bias; Grobys survivor-momentum fragility; data-integrity failures.
key_caveat: Fail as deployable alpha after data-quality and cost gates.

label: Cryptocurrency volatility / risk forecasting
summary: Crypto volatility is forecastable with robust GARCH/realized methods. This is risk forecasting, not return alpha.
positive_evidence: Trucíos robust GARCH dominance; ML vol studies with mixed incremental gains.
negative_evidence: Single-asset/early-regime limits; ML vol heterogeneity.
key_caveat: Pass for risk forecasting only.

label: Crypto venue fragmentation / apparent arbitrage
summary: Large cross-venue gaps are real but often inside no-arbitrage bounds once transfer latency, capital controls, and default risk are priced.
positive_evidence: Makarov-Schoar fragmentation; wash-trading volume contamination evidence.
negative_evidence: Quoted gaps ≠ executable riskless profit; wash trading contaminates volume-based predictors.
key_caveat: Structural fact, not a validated retail arbitrage strategy.

label: Cryptocurrency return machine learning
summary: Reported OOS ML fits often rely on lagged returns, microcaps, and incomplete delist/cost treatment.
positive_evidence: Some chronological ML papers report positive OOS R² / cost-adjusted portfolios.
negative_evidence: Implausible magnitudes, data integrity issues, and no strong independent net replication.
key_caveat: Research only under the strict standard.

label: Listed REIT return predictability
summary: Gross REIT persistence exists historically, but OOS and cost-adjusted tests are mostly null or fragile. Dynamic model averaging finds only pockets of value.
positive_evidence: Some DMA/regime models report OOS utility pockets.
negative_evidence: Nelling-Gyourko and Ling-Naranjo-Ryngaert show costs erase gains; 1990s OOS largely absent.
key_caveat: Net return predictability not established for listed REITs.

label: REIT volatility forecasting
summary: High-frequency realized moments and global conditions improve REIT volatility forecasts.
positive_evidence: Skew/kurtosis HAR gains; GARCH-MIDAS global-condition gains.
negative_evidence: Overlapping-author lines and no prospective risk-decision test.
key_caveat: Risk forecasting supported; not return alpha.

label: Private equity reported-performance persistence
summary: Using only information available at fundraising, buyout persistence largely disappears post-2000; VC persistence remains but declines. Appraisal/NAV smoothing makes reported returns noncomparable to public markets.
positive_evidence: Narrower VC persistence at decision date; interim marks contain some information.
negative_evidence: Buyout persistence fades; NAV manipulation around fundraising; smoothing inflates Sharpe and autocorrelation.
key_caveat: Conditional VC selection feature, not public-market-style predictability.

label: Forecast combinations / shrinkage / 1/N benchmarks
scope: Equities, bonds, commodities allocation and forecasting
summary: Combinations and shrinkage improve stability versus overfit single models. Complex optimizers often fail to beat 1/N after estimation error and turnover.
positive_evidence: Combination and economically motivated shrinkage evidence; Kozak SDF shrinkage OOS.
negative_evidence: DeMiguel 1/N benchmark failures for many optimizers.
key_caveat: Supported as variance control/regularization, not universal alpha.

label: Time-series foundation models for financial returns
summary: Off-the-shelf TSFMs do not reliably beat strong econometric or tree baselines for returns; any gains are sample-efficiency / calibration effects, not proven net alpha.
positive_evidence: Occasional rank wins or fine-tuning gains in narrow settings.
negative_evidence: Random-walk and linear/transformer competitiveness; weak significance and no economic validation.
key_caveat: Reject zero-shot TSFMs as a default financial return forecaster.

label: Alternative data (satellite / search / proprietary panels)
summary: Satellite and similar alternative datasets can contain incremental fundamental information, but vendor drift, acquisition cost, and independent replication block strong effectiveness claims. Search-based signals are fragile.
positive_evidence: JFQA satellite parking-lot evidence; early Google Trends associations.
negative_evidence: Proprietary panels prevent independent recreation; Google Trends results are questioned/fragile.
key_caveat: Commercially plausible, scientifically thin for public verification.

label: Forecast evaluation, real-time vintages, and backtest integrity
summary: Proper forecast comparison, vintage data, proper scores, and overfitting corrections are prerequisites for any effectiveness claim. These methods do not themselves produce alpha.
positive_evidence: Diebold-Mariano, Giacomini-White, proper scores, deflated Sharpe, real-time vintages, and multiple-testing frameworks are widely replicated methods.
negative_evidence: Not applicable as market-predictability alpha evidence.
key_caveat: Methodological backbone for rating other families; not a trading strategy.
